title: Imports point inward through the layer hierarchy

facts.note: Non-test source files; test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Layer read from the file path's layer segment, in commons and feature code alike; files without a layer segment are out of scope.
Observer must resolve each project (non-bare-npm) import of an in-scope file to its target layer, covering every affected import, not only newly added ones.

fires: A domain module imports an application, integration, presentation or assembly module.
An application module imports from presentation or integration.
An integration module imports from presentation.
A feature module (not only commons) has an import whose target layer is outward of its own layer.
A change moves or edits code so that an existing import of an in-scope file is affected.
doesNotFire: The composition root (assembly) imports any layer to wire them together.
A test file imports across layers.
Files under vendored or build directories.
A bare npm package specifier import (outside the project graph).
A file whose path carries no layer segment.

given: A non-test Bun source module (commons or feature) whose path has a layer segment
then: The import MUST point inward: presentation -> application -> domain; integration -> application, domain; only assembly (the composition root) may reach any layer.
prefer: When an inner layer needs an outer capability, use an existing inward-facing port.
During GREEN: introduce the smallest missing port only when the current behavior cannot otherwise be implemented correctly, and limit its contract to what the acceptance requires.
avoid: Reclassifying or merging layers merely to make one import legal.
Adding an outward-pointing dependency as a temporary step.
Spreading 'knows everything' wiring outside the composition root.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file with no layer segment is outside these rules, not in violation.
why: It governs feature code too, where most layering damage happens. The assembly exemption makes it workable: something must know about everything, and confining that to the composition root is the point of having one.
evidence: Every affected import still points in an allowed direction (no bun_clean_architecture_detector finding).
verifier_detail: Resolves each import to its target layer and flags an edge the hierarchy does not permit.
Allowed edges (inward_import): presentation -> application -> domain; integration -> application, domain. The permitted direction.
assembly_exemption: the composition root's freedom to reach any layer.
Skip test files and vendored/build directories; skip bare npm specifiers; files with no layer segment are out of scope, not violations.
Validator ref: bun_clean_architecture_detector. Severity 3, disposition strict.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
This is the general rule the commons rules apply to one tree.

sharedNodes.text: During GREEN: reuse the nearest existing compliant dependency path. Do not broaden: do not redesign adjacent modules. Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.

additions.text: Spreading 'knows everything' wiring outside the composition root.
additions.justification: Restates the source reasoning (S013, S017) as an anti-pattern; no new obligation beyond the hierarchy itself.

additions.text: A change affecting an existing import of an in-scope file.
additions.justification: Source requires every affected import to remain allowed (S031) and resolves each import (S014); clarifies activation is not limited to newly added imports.

trace.note: Heading for the canonical path, expressed by then + prefer[0].
Canonical inward direction incl. assembly wiring all layers is exactly the then obligation.
GREEN qualifier carried in prefer[1] text and the shared phase-loop node.
Do not broaden heading; rule-specific items in avoid, generic item in shared node.
Prove heading, expressed by the evidence array.
